extracted.intended_audience: researchers, data stewards, librarians, repository managers, and institutions implementing or assessing FAIR data
extracted.subtask_short: FAIR data implementation for research datasets
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and concrete criteria for making digital research data and metadata Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR), plus related implementation/assessment notes. Useful for data managers, policy makers, and tool builders who must plan, implement, or evaluate FAIRness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findable — general
rubrics_metrics.description: The first step in (re)using data is to find them. Metadata and data should be easy to find for both humans and computers; machine-readable metadata are essential for automatic discovery of datasets and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises discoverability for humans and automated systems; FAIRification requires creating metadata that supports search and discovery workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: F1: Globally unique and persistent identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data are assigned a globally unique and persistent identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifiers should be persistent (e.g., DOIs, PURLs) so both humans and machines can unambiguously reference the digital object over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: F2: Rich metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Data are described with rich metadata (defined by R1 below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide extensive descriptive metadata that supports discovery and reuse; richness is defined in part by the Reusable (R1) criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: F3: Metadata includes the data identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata clearly and explicitly include the identifier of the data they describe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the metadata record contains the canonical identifier for the data object so linkage and retrieval are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: F4: Registered/indexed in searchable resource
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data are registered or indexed in a searchable resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish metadata to catalogs, registries, or search indices so that datasets appear in search results and discovery services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the user finds the required data, they need to know how they can be accessed, possibly including authentication and authorisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility covers both the means of retrieval and any access control procedures; metadata should explain access conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: A1: Retrievable by identifier via standardised protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data are retrievable by their identifier using a standardised communications protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use widely-adopted protocols (HTTP, OAI-PMH, FTP, etc.) so machines can retrieve data/metadata programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: A1.1: Protocol is open, free, and universally implementable
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol is open, free, and universally implementable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer open protocols without proprietary constraints to maximise broad technical access and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: A1.2: Protocol allows authentication and authorisation where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol allows for an authentication and authorisation procedure, where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support secure access mechanisms alongside open protocols to accommodate controlled-access datasets while remaining machine-actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: A2: Metadata remain accessible if data are no longer available
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata are accessible, even when the data are no longer available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persistent metadata records enable discovery and provenance tracking even after datasets are withdrawn or removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperable — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Data need to be integrated with other data and interoperate with applications or workflows for analysis, storage, and processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interoperability targets both syntactic and semantic compatibility so tools and workflows can combine datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: I1: Use formal, accessible, shared language for knowledge representation
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data use a formal, accessible, shared, and broadly applicable language for knowledge representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt standard representation formats (RDF, JSON-LD, XML, etc.) and ontologies to enable machine interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: I2: Use vocabularies that follow FAIR principles
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data use vocabularies that follow FAIR principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlled vocabularies/ontologies that are themselves findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable to avoid ad hoc terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: I3: Include qualified references to other metadata/data
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data include qualified references to other (meta)data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link datasets and metadata explicitly (e.g., provenance, related resources) using qualified relations so machines can navigate relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusable — general
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate goal of FAIR is to optimise the reuse of data. Metadata and data should be well-described so that they can be replicated and/or combined in different settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on clear licensing, provenance, and community standards to enable downstream reuse and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: R1: Richly described with accurate and relevant attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data are richly described with a plurality of accurate and relevant attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the descriptive, technical, and contextual metadata necessary for understanding and reuse (e.g., variables, units, experimental context).

rubrics_metrics.name: R1.1: Released with clear and accessible data usage license
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data are released with a clear and accessible data usage license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicit machine-readable licensing (e.g., CC0, CC-BY) so users and machines understand reuse rights; this is also the basis of 'FAIR/O' when open licenses are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: R1.2: Associated with detailed provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data are associated with detailed provenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record origin, processing steps, and responsible agents so others can assess fitness for use and reproduce workflows where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: R1.3: Meet domain-relevant community standards
rubrics_metrics.description: (Meta)data meet domain-relevant community standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow disciplinary metadata schemas, reporting guidelines, and formats so data are interoperable and reusable within the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-actionability
rubrics_metrics.description: FAIR principles emphasize machine-actionability: computational systems must be able to find, access, interoperate, and reuse data with none or minimal human intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design metadata, identifiers, protocols, and vocabularies so that processes and workflows can operate automatically; this underpins many specific FAIR criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR/O: FAIR plus explicit open license
rubrics_metrics.description: The abbreviation FAIR/O data indicates the dataset or database complies with FAIR principles and also carries an explicit data-capable open license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If openness is desired, ensure the license permits machine-readable reuse; otherwise document access/licensing clearly (see R1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure linkage (registration/indexing & preservation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles refer to data, metadata, and infrastructure; e.g., F4 defines that metadata and data are registered or indexed in a searchable resource (infrastructure component).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider repositories, registries, indices, and preservation services as part of FAIR implementation; technical infrastructure must support the FAIR criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Data Maturity Model (assessment guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 2020 FAIR Data Maturity Model provides specification and guidelines for assessing 'FAIRness'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Maturity Model's metrics and assessment guidance to operationalise and evaluate FAIR criteria rather than relying on informal judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation cost guidance for data management plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides on implementing FAIR data practices state that the cost of a data management plan in compliance with FAIR practices should be ~5% of the total research budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an implementation-level recommendation to help planning and budgeting for FAIRification activities (curation, metadata, repository fees, staff time).

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE Principles as complementary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance complement FAIR by adding Collective benefit, Authority to control, Responsibility, and Ethics to ensure guidelines address historical contexts and power differentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where data involve Indigenous or other sovereign communities, consider CARE alongside FAIR — FAIR does not replace ethical, legal, or governance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: FAIRness is challenging to implement and assess
rubrics_metrics.description: Making data FAIR is challenging, and assessing FAIRness is itself difficult; different communities interpret FAIR differently which leads to inconsistent implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect variation across disciplines; adopt community standards, use maturity models, and document interpretation choices to improve consistency.
